_note: Canonical user-story catalogue for Project Io — the authoritative index of WHAT THE PLAYER
IS TRYING TO DO, decomposed by player intent rather than by system or by feature.
One story = one object in `stories`. USER_STORIES.md is the readable mirror (JSON wins on
any disagreement, exactly as backlog.json wins over BACKLOG.md).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS — the second route from docs to code.
The design docs decompose the game by SYSTEM/SURFACE ('what is this thing?').
backlog.json decomposes it by FEATURE ('what do we build next?').
Neither decomposes it by PLAYER INTENT — an orthogonal axis. This catalogue is that axis.
A story traced DOWNWARD (-> UI surface -> backlog item -> requirement) and UPWARD
(-> system -> pillar) turns intent into a COVERAGE check: a story no surface serves is a
gap to fill; a shipped feature no story needs is scope to justify. That check is the value
the feature-backlog structurally cannot give.
A PILLAR OF TESTING. Each story's `requirements` are the brief slugs in req/requirements.json
whose rows carry executable verification (visual/golden, headless, code). The story is the
player-goal framing; the linked briefs are how you PROVE the goal still holds after a change.
A story with a real requirement link is a walkable, testable acceptance path — walk it (BL-098)
or re-run its briefs (verifier-* skills). A `served` story whose briefs go red is a regression
against a player goal, caught on the intent axis rather than the feature axis.
RELATIONSHIP TO BL-098. BL-098 ('UX review from the perspective of user stories') is the
REVIEW ACTIVITY — walk each story through the live UI and produce a friction list. This file
is the ARTIFACT that review consumes. Build the catalogue here; run BL-098 against it.
COVERAGE (the served-state axis; distinct from the backlog's design-state ✓/~):
served  (glyph ●) — the goal has a working home in the UI + code today.
partial (glyph ◐) — partly served; a friction point or a missing step remains.
gap     (glyph ○) — no home yet; a real hole in the software.
planned (glyph ◇) — deliberately outside current scope (e.g. Conflict) or queued.
FIELDS.
id         — US-XXX, parallel to BL-XXX.
cluster    — one of `clusters[].id`; the player-goal grouping this story belongs to.
title      — short human name.
story      — the canonical 'As the player, I want ... so that ...' sentence.
coverage   — served | partial | gap | planned (see vocab above).
glyph      — mirrors coverage 1:1 for skimming.
traces     — the load-bearing links that make this a ROUTE, not just prose:
pillars       (up)   — Trade | Conflict, from CONCEPT/SYSTEMS.
systems       (up)   — SYSTEMS.md system names.
surfaces      (down) — {doc, surface} the UI element(s) that serve the goal.
backlog       (down) — BL-XXX ids that realise or affect the story.
requirements  (down) — req/requirements.json brief slugs that verify it ([] = link owed).
walkthrough — the end-to-end flow BL-098 walks; ordered steps.
friction    — known rough edges feeding BL-098 ('' if none noted).
written     — capture date (absolute; newest-dated wins on conflict).
testing     — {mode, note}. mode = manual | auto | mixed. HOW this story is verified:
manual — strategic / UX-judgment; walk it live (the BL-098 activity).
auto   — its requirement briefs carry runnable (golden/headless) verification; re-run them.
mixed  — an automatable core plus a manual read on top. Enforced by tools/session/story_check.js:
a story declared `auto`/`mixed` must have >=1 brief with runnable verification.
SCOPE HONESTY. The `clusters` taxonomy maps the WHOLE game's intent so the axis is complete,
but `stories` stay within prototype scope (economy loop). Post-prototype clusters (Conflict)
are present and marked `scope: post-prototype`, deliberately unpopulated — do not author
out-of-scope stories (io-standing-rules § Scope & sequence).
COVERAGE STATE (2026-07-05). Legacy-feature pass: 12 stories spanning all seven prototype
clusters, every story requirement-linked. This baselines the shipped player-facing features
(lenses, navigation, time, build, recipe/workforce, sell, convoys, survey, rivals, population)
as `served`. Next passes: fill secondary stories, and build the coverage-audit tool (a check
that flags served stories with dead links, and backlog items in no story).

clusters.name: Get my bearings
clusters.intent: Know who I am, where I am, and what I could do next; move around the world and control its clock.

clusters.name: Find opportunity
clusters.intent: See where to grow — good ground, unmet demand, room to expand — at a glance, without arming anything.

clusters.name: Build
clusters.intent: Pick a tile, understand what I can build and why-not, place it, and steer what it produces.

clusters.name: Run my economy
clusters.intent: Know whether my assets make money, what my runway is, and why my workforce is constrained.

clusters.name: Expand & explore
clusters.intent: Survey a new body, judge whether it's worth the cost and time, and reach it.

clusters.name: Move goods & read demand
clusters.intent: Govern how my stock is released, ship it between bodies, and see where demand and price sit.

clusters.name: Read the competition
clusters.intent: Infer what rivals are doing from public signals — buildings, market prints, activity — without seeing their books.

clusters.name: Contest territory
clusters.intent: Claim, defend, and invade ground; make an opponent's supply lines a target.

stories.title: Know who and where I am on load, and what I could do next
stories.story: As the player, when the campaign loads I want to see who I am, where my home is, and what my first move could be, so that I get my bearings before touching anything.

surfaces.surface: Profile panel (corp identity + emblem) and header balance
Solar canvas opening focus + home-body marker + HQ pip
Selection element ('what's my move here?')

walkthrough: Campaign loads -> the view opens focused on the player's home body (BL-085 initial focus).
The Profile panel shows the corp identity + emblem (BL-090); the header shows the balance.
An always-on 'you are here' marker + HQ pip distinguishes home from rivals (BL-085/BL-092).
The player selects home -> the Selection element frames the current state and available actions.
stories.friction: The 'what could I do next' half is the weak leg: identity/where landed with BL-085/BL-090/BL-092, but the opening view does not actively suggest a first move. Candidate BL-098 finding — an orient-time next-action nudge.

testing.note: The orient / first-move experience is a UX judgment — walk it live. Presence + emblem renders are golden-backed, but 'what's my move next?' is the point.

stories.title: Pick a tile, see what I can build, its cost and why-not, and build it
stories.story: As the player, I want to select a tile and see what I can build there, what it costs in budget and materials, and why I can't build the things I can't, so that I can commit a construction in a few clicks with no guessing.

surfaces.surface: Single-click a tile to select it
Tile Selection element -> 'Construct Buildings' button
Tile construction ledger — placeable list with cost + reason-coded why-not + Build (BL-162)

walkthrough: Single-click a tile on the Planetary canvas -> the Selection element reads the tile (per-resource production graphs, terrain, deposits) without arming anything (BL-123).
Click 'Construct Buildings' -> the tile construction ledger opens in the fold-out column (BL-162), listing every building type placeable on this tile; the player balance heads the list.
Each option shows its budget + material cost (e.g. '100 cr, 20 Stl') — extraction per deposited resource, plus processing / port / launchpad (and roads / logistics, BL-147-149).
Options that can't be placed show the reason instead of a Build button — e.g. 'A port must sit on the coast' (BL-071 reason vocabulary); unaffordable options disable Build with 'Can't afford'.
Click 'Build' on a valid, affordable option -> the construction is enqueued on the tile and the cost debited (the same construct_building path a canvas placement uses).
stories.friction: First pass (BL-162): building images are placeholders and a per-candidate expected-profit chart is owed. The old arm-placement-on-canvas flow and its panel-occlusion issue (BL-082) are retired — the construction ledger is the single build surface now.

testing.note: Fresh-start buildability asserted end-to-end by scripts/verify/fresh_start_build.lua; the construction ledger itself is captured by scripts/verify/tile_build_ledger.lua (land + water tiles — cost + reason-coded why-not). Cost debit + placement legality are headless (construction-pricing, building-placement-rules, market-stockpile-build-gate).

stories.title: Know whether a building makes money and what my runway is
stories.story: As the player, I want to know whether a given building is profitable and whether I can afford my next moves, without hunting across ledgers, so that I can act before bankruptcy rather than discover it.

surfaces.surface: Budget ledger — profit chart + top-8 buildings-by-profit rank table (BL-171)
Per-building profitability read on selection (BL-074)
Economy panel — balance / income / expenditure trend plots (BL-066)

walkthrough: Open the Budget ledger (nav rail 'Budget') -> a profit line chart shows profit per econ tick, and a top-8 buildings-by-profit table shows which assets carry their weight, with a rank-change-vs-a-year-ago column (BL-171).
Select a building -> its per-building profitability (revenue vs. running cost) also reads on the Selection element (BL-074).
The Economy panel's balance / income / expenditure trend plots (BL-066) show the trajectory — 'am I improving?'.

GAP: 'how long until I'm underwater?' — the projected runway (and the itemised cashflow breakdown, BL-072) were removed from the Budget ledger in the BL-171 redesign (deferred to a dedicated breakdown menu); today runway must be inferred from the balance + the header net-per-quarter figure.
stories.friction: The BL-171 redesign traded the itemised cashflow table + projected runway for a profit chart + rank table (Ben's call — too much detail at a glance). The 'makes money' leg is now well-served (profit chart + rank table); the 'what's my runway' leg is a GAP until the deferred breakdown menu lands — re-home the runway there (BL-155-adjacent).

testing.note: Per-building profitability is a headless invariant (per-building-profitability); the Budget ledger layout — profit chart + rank table — is golden-backed (budget-ledger-redesign: scripts/verify/balance_ledger.lua + budget_ledger_ranked.lua). The runway leg has no home today, so it is a manual note, not a passing check.

stories.title: Navigate the zoom ladder — from the system down to a tile and back
stories.story: As the player, I want to drill from the solar view down to a single tile and climb back out, so that I can move fluidly between the strategic and the local without losing my place.

surfaces.surface: Zoom ladder — Solar / Circumplanetary / Planetary; click a body to descend
Minimap chrome — click to ascend a rung
Selection 'go to' descends to the Planetary surface

walkthrough: On the Solar canvas the player clicks a body -> the view descends to its Circumplanetary / Planetary canvas.
Entity markers on the surface are hit-testable; a single click selects, a double click navigates (BL-031/BL-059).
The Selection element's 'go to' descends straight to a tile on the Planetary surface.
The player clicks the minimap to climb back up a rung, without losing selection context.
stories.friction: The click-model (single selects / double navigates) must stay consistent across all three canvases; a divergence here is a prime BL-098 finding since the ladder is the most-repeated player motion.

testing.note: The single-selects / double-navigates click-model must FEEL consistent across all three canvases; hit-testing is code-backed but the feel is manual.

stories.title: Control the flow of time — pause, resume, and change speed
stories.story: As the player, I want to pause, resume, change the simulation speed, and read the clock, so that I can slow down for a decision and speed through the quiet stretches.

surfaces.surface: Calendar block + speed buttons (Roman-numeral labels) + econ-tick progress bar
In-app system menu Pause/Resume (Esc parity)

walkthrough: The player reads the calendar block (date + tick cadence) to know where they are in time.
They press a speed button (I/II/III) or pause; the econ-tick progress bar shows how close the next resolution is.
The corner gear / Esc opens the system menu for Pause/Resume without touching the keyboard hotkeys.
stories.friction: Pause reachability landed twice (hotkey + gear menu, BL-070); confirm they agree and that the current speed is legible at a glance, not inferred from motion.

testing.note: Speed states and pause reachability are mechanical (time-speed-curve, in-app-system-menu).

stories.title: See where to grow at a glance, without arming build mode
stories.story: As the player, I want to read where opportunity is — good ground, dense industry, unmet demand — from the map alone, so that I can decide where to expand before committing to build mode.

surfaces.surface: Opportunity (net-margin), Industry (substrate), Scarcity, Production lenses on the control strip
Per-tile lens tint on the Planetary surface

walkthrough: The player selects the Opportunity lens -> tiles tint by net margin, showing where a chain would pay (BL-086).
They switch to the Industry lens -> the nation-owned substrate reads as a throughput field, showing where activity already concentrates (BL-084).
The Scarcity lens (per resource) shows where a good is absent -> unmet local demand.
None of this requires arming build mode, so reading and deciding stay separate from committing.
stories.friction: Several lenses answer 'where to grow' from different angles; the risk is the player not knowing which lens answers which question. A lens colour-scheme pass (BL-016, design-owed) is the open refinement.

testing.note: Every lens is a golden-verified render (opportunity-ambient, industry-lens, scarcity-lens-render, production-output-lens); re-bless on deliberate visual change.

stories.title: Set a building's recipe and workforce target
stories.story: As the player, I want to choose what an existing building produces and how much workforce it draws, so that I can steer my production to what the market needs rather than accept a fixed output.

surfaces.surface: Per-building recipe + workforce controls on selection
Recipe tables + workforce scalar model

walkthrough: The player selects a building -> its current recipe and workforce target read on the Selection element.
They change the recipe -> the economy honours the new recipe at the next tick (golden-verified).
They raise the workforce target -> output scales, capped by local habitability-gated workforce (BL-041).
If workforce is short, the cap is shown as the reason, not a silent shortfall.
stories.friction: The workforce cap (habitability) and the target interact; the player needs to see 'you asked for X, the body allows Y' in one place. Ties into US-012 (population legibility).

testing.note: 'Recipe honoured next tick' is golden-verified (building-management); the workforce cap is headless (habitability-workforce).

stories.title: Govern how my stock is released — standing sell orders with a floor
stories.story: As the player, I want to place standing sell orders with a floor price and bias which counterparties I match, so that I control how my goods reach market instead of dumping everything at the cleared price.

surfaces.surface: Trade pillar — standing sell orders (per body/resource qty + floor); preferential purchasing
Market ledger — order book + auto-sell/auto-buy health

walkthrough: The player sets a standing sell order for a (body, resource): a quantity and a floor price.
At market clearing the order is honoured ahead of the anonymous auto-sell path, so stock is not dumped below the floor.
Preferential purchasing lets a buyer bias which seller it matches (BL-037).
The warm-start / Market ledger surfaces auto-buy vs auto-sell health so the player sees whether their stock is moving.
stories.friction: Sell orders, the anonymous auto-sell path, and the order book are three release mechanisms; the ledger must make clear which one moved a given unit, or profitability reads (US-003) become hard to trust.

testing.note: Order clearing + floor precedence are econ-harness invariants (player-sell-orders, order-book); ledger surfacing is golden (multi-market-dashboard).

stories.title: Move goods between bodies and see where they flow
stories.story: As the player, I want to ship goods from where they're cheap to where they're dear and see the lanes that carry them, so that I can profit from spatial price differences net of logistics.

surfaces.surface: Convoy layer — dispatch, logistics cost, arrival crediting
Market lens (boundaries + price readout) and Scarcity lens
Persistent trade routes drawn from convoy traffic

walkthrough: Terrestrial shortfalls auto-dispatch a convoy from the cheapest reachable source; the cargo leaves the source pool at dispatch (BL-039).
The convoy advances per tick and credits the destination on arrival, so the two bodies' prices converge net of logistics cost.
Space launches are always player-directed (never auto), gated on a Launchpad + Orbital Port and Era 1.
Persistent trade routes record the lanes (BL-088); the Market lens shows catchment boundaries and prices.
stories.friction: Logistics cost is what makes distant arbitrage marginal; the player needs the per-unit landed cost visible at decision time, or the 'is this trade worth it?' judgement is guesswork.

testing.note: Convoy logistics + spatial price convergence are headless (supply-layer); 'landed cost visible at decision time' is a manual read.

stories.title: Read what a rival is doing from public signals
stories.story: As the player, I want to infer a competitor's activity from what's public — their buildings, market prints, and commercial activity — without seeing their books, so that I can respond to rivals I can't directly observe.

surfaces.surface: Visibility rule (buildings public, production/stockpile private) + route-driven activity fog
Rival building selection shows public facts only
Hover-card body activity line — market pulse when known+

walkthrough: The player sees a rival's buildings on-canvas but selecting one reveals only public facts — no production rate or stockpile (BL-068).
A body carries an activity tier (Unknown/Known/Stale/Visible) lit by the player's own routes and presence (BL-089).
Hovering a known+ body surfaces its market pulse on the hover card (BL-100).
Market prices and supply/demand aggregates are the public channel the player reasons from.
stories.friction: The activity fog and the geographic survey fog are independent axes (a body can be Known-but-unsurveyed); the UI must not conflate them. The proximity-glimpse refinement (BL-099, designed) is the open follow-on.

testing.note: Inferring a rival from public signals is strategic judgment; the visibility RULE (public/private) is code-checkable but the read itself is manual.

stories.title: Survey a new body and judge whether it's worth it
stories.story: As the player, I want to preview a survey's cost and time, dispatch it, and watch a body reveal region by region, so that I can decide whether an unknown body is worth investing in before I commit.

surfaces.surface: Survey system — geographic fog, region-by-region reveal
Per-body survey badge
Survey section — cost/ETA preview + live progress
Unrevealed regions masked until scanned

walkthrough: The player selects an unsurveyed body -> the Selection panel shows only its type, orbit, and grid size.
The Survey section previews cost and ETA, both scaling with body size and distance from home.
The player dispatches -> credits are debited upfront; a transit phase reveals nothing, then a scan phase reveals the surface one region at a time in deterministic order.
Deposit richness bands (rich/moderate/sparse) resolve; exact amounts wait for first extraction placement.
stories.friction: Cost is charged upfront before any reveal; the preview must make the gamble legible ('you pay N now, first tiles in T ticks') so a survey never feels like money vanished.

testing.note: Survey determinism + cost/ETA scaling are headless (survey-system); the 'is it worth it?' preview legibility is a manual walk.

stories.title: Understand why my workforce is constrained
stories.story: As the player, I want to see why workforce is limited on a body and where population concentrates, so that I can make siting decisions by reason rather than by guesswork.

surfaces.surface: Habitability -> workforce feedback
Population / Habitability lens
Habitability -> workforce reasoning on hover / selection

walkthrough: The player selects the Population lens -> tiles tint by habitability, showing where labour can be sustained.
Population centres draw as tiered, named settlements (BL-083), so the workforce source is visible on the map.
Selecting a building or tile surfaces the habitability -> workforce chain: why the cap is what it is (BL-069).
The player sites new extraction/processing where workforce can actually reach it.
stories.friction: The workforce cap surfaced here is the same cap US-007 hits when raising a workforce target; the two surfaces must tell one consistent story about the ceiling.

testing.note: Population lens + centre markers are golden (population-lens-render, pop-centre-markers); the habitability->workforce cap is headless (population-legibility).

stories.title: Judge how good a specific tile is for production before I build
stories.story: As the player, I want to see how productive a specific tile would be — its output relative to the rest of the map — before I commit a building, so that I build on strong ground rather than guessing from raw deposit numbers.

surfaces.surface: Tile Selection element — per-resource production graphs, this tile vs the 10th-percentile tile (BL-123)

walkthrough: Single-click a tile on the Planetary canvas -> the Selection element opens on that tile.

For each resource deposited on the tile, a stacked bar reads the tile's own production (hazard-adjusted yield) against the 10th-percentile tile for that resource (BL-123) — a strong tile towers over the P10 reference, a weak one barely clears it.
The scrollable graph list covers every deposited resource, so the tile's whole production profile is legible before any build decision.
The player carries that read into 'Construct Buildings' (US-002) to commit on strong ground.
stories.friction: Complements the at-a-glance lens read (US-006): the lens says WHERE broadly, these per-tile graphs say HOW GOOD this exact tile is. Only the prototype-extractable resources (iron ore / petroleum / water / agricultural produce) become buildable extraction; other deposits (stone, timber) show a production bar but no extraction option yet — a legible-but-inert read.

testing.note: The tile production graphs are golden-backed (tile-selection-layout: scripts/verify/selection_tile_layout.lua, single-deposit + multi-deposit built tile). Whether the Tile-vs-P10 framing actually guides a build decision is a manual UX read (walk it, BL-098).
